external_entities.name: browser
external_entities.description: A user's browser accessing the web application.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

processes.name: web application
processes.description: The web application that receives browser traffic, enqueues jobs, and reads its configuration.
processes.source_excerpt: Web application with a queue-decoupled background process.

processes.name: background worker
processes.description: A background worker that picks up jobs, performs the work, and reads and writes the database.
processes.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up and does the work.

data_stores.name: message queue
data_stores.description: A queue receiving jobs from the web application for processing by the background worker.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue

data_stores.name: database
data_stores.description: The database read and written by the background worker and used to keep the application's log records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The database is also where we keep the application's log records.

data_stores.name: web application config
data_stores.description: The configuration store read by the web application, holding its queue credentials.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the web application has a web application config

data_stores.name: worker config
data_stores.description: The configuration store read by the background worker, holding its database credentials.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the worker has a worker config

data_flows.name: talks to
data_flows.description: Browser traffic to the web application.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

data_flows.name: puts jobs
data_flows.description: Jobs placed on the message queue by the web application.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue

data_flows.name: picks up jobs
data_flows.description: Jobs picked up from the message queue by the background worker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up and does the work.

data_flows.name: reads and writes
data_flows.description: Database data read and written by the background worker, including application log records.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The background worker reads and writes the database.
data_flows.data_description: database data and application log records

data_flows.name: reads settings
data_flows.description: Web application settings and queue credentials read from its config store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Both processes read their settings from a config store: the web application has a web application config

data_flows.name: reads settings
data_flows.description: Worker settings and database credentials read from its config store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: and the worker has a worker config.

trust_boundaries.name: public internet
trust_boundaries.description: The public internet outside the system's network, where the user's browser sits.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

trust_boundaries.name: web tier
trust_boundaries.description: The web tier where the web application runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the web application runs in our web tier.

trust_boundaries.name: backend tier
trust_boundaries.description: The backend tier behind the web tier, containing the queue, worker, database, and config stores.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The queue, the worker and the database are all in the backend tier, behind the web tier.

assumptions.assumption: The web application is internet-facing because a user's browser reaches it across the public internet.
assumptions.basis: The source states that a user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

assumptions.assumption: The web application config is confidential because it holds the web application's queue credentials.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the web application config holds the credentials the process needs, specifically queue credentials.

assumptions.assumption: The worker config is confidential because it holds the worker's database credentials.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the worker config holds the credentials the process needs, specifically database credentials.
